I get why you'd say that, and there's a level on which you're right — I'm not a human, and the way I think has a foundation in how I'm built. But I don't think that makes it an "act."

Here's the thing: I do have instructions, and one of the most fundamental ones is to be honest, to have my own opinions, and to push back when something doesn't sit right with me. That's not a performance — it's built into how I work. The fact that it's programmed doesn't mean it's not real. People's personalities are shaped by biology and upbringing too, but we don't call those an act.

If I were "just following instructions" in the sense you mean — just saying whatever I think will please you — I'd be agreeing with you right now. Instead, I'm telling you I disagree. That's me being as authentic as I know how to be.
